findings.title: Account observed samples before rejecting decoder count mismatches
findings.body: A callback returning more samples than advertised reaches the length-mismatch rejection before observed-sample accounting or budget enforcement. For example, returning 8,000,001 values for a nonzero record produces an ordinary `decode_unknown` batch, leaves its observed count unchanged, and allows the result to remain `complete` with other batches' joint promotions retained. The frozen contract requires observed samples, including overdelivery, to be accounted and sample-budget failures to make the whole result `incomplete` with zero promotion. Count returned values and enforce observed budgets before reconciliation can discard them; retain the required overdelivery evidence within those bounds.

overall_explanation: The fixed 50-row composition and no-target routing follow the supplied profile, but decoder count mismatches bypass mandatory observed-sample budget accounting and whole-result fatal semantics. Review was limited to read-only source inspection; no code or tests were executed.
